description: Decode-level pin-store cases carrying RAW WIRE TEXT. Each runtime feeds these exact bytes through its own load-and-validate path, because a corpus of pre-decoded typed structures cannot express a malformed document at all - the harness would die loading the test data instead of reporting the rejection the case exists to assert. Expectations are POSITIVE PER RUNTIME and include error substrings, not outcomes alone: two runtimes can reject the same document for entirely different reasons, which reads as agreement while hiding a real divergence. That is how the non-string-key divergence below was found. No field here selects which assertion runs; 'divergence' is prose for the reader and is never branched on.

cases.name: valid-baseline
cases.yaml:
pins:
  did:key:zA:
    address: acme.com/alice
    first_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    last_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
addresses:
  acme.com/alice: did:key:zA

error_substrings: store is empty or has no document
pin store is empty or has no document
store is empty or has no document
pin store is empty or has no document
store is empty or has no document
pin store is empty or has no document

cases.name: multi-document-framing
cases.yaml:
pins:
  did:key:zA:
    address: acme.com/alice
    first_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    last_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"

---
pins: {}
addresses: {}

error_substrings: store must be a single document
expected a single document in the stream

  nested: [1, 2]

    last_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    future_pin_key: keep-me
addresses:

cases.name: merge-key
cases.note: The merge value is an INLINE mapping with no anchor. An earlier version used '<<: *anchor', which both runtimes rejected at their ANCHOR guard before the merge-key guard ran — so the case passed while testing nothing it was named for, and disabling either merge-key check left the whole corpus green. Keep this fixture anchor-free.
cases.yaml:
pins:
  did:key:zA:
    <<:
      server: s1
    address: acme.com/alice
    first_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    last_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
addresses:
  acme.com/alice: did:key:zA

error_substrings: must not use YAML merge keys
must not use merge keys

cases.name: non-string-pin-key-consistently-referenced
cases.divergence: DIVERGENCE (measured, not aspirational). Go rejects non-string mapping keys (the aajc.9a strictness); js-yaml coerces them to their string form and TypeScript accepts. Recorded per runtime so the difference is visible rather than hidden. Not reachable through our own write path - aw is the sole writer and never emits a non-string key - so it requires a hand-edit, a third-party tool, or a crafted file. Tightening TypeScript is tracked separately; the naive fix is wrong because non-string scalar VALUES are legitimate here (Pin.log_seq is a number, and unknown-field preservation accepts arbitrary nested values), so any tightening must distinguish keys from values.
cases.yaml:
pins:
  12345:
    address: acme.com/alice
    first_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    last_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
addresses:
  acme.com/alice: "12345"

error_substrings: has a key that is not a plain string

cases.name: non-string-address-key
cases.divergence: DIVERGENCE (measured, not aspirational). Go rejects non-string mapping keys (the aajc.9a strictness); js-yaml coerces them to their string form and TypeScript accepts. Recorded per runtime so the difference is visible rather than hidden. Not reachable through our own write path - aw is the sole writer and never emits a non-string key - so it requires a hand-edit, a third-party tool, or a crafted file. Tightening TypeScript is tracked separately; the naive fix is wrong because non-string scalar VALUES are legitimate here (Pin.log_seq is a number, and unknown-field preservation accepts arbitrary nested values), so any tightening must distinguish keys from values. The pin's address is the numeric key itself so that the forward and reverse indexes agree once the key is coerced: both runtimes now check index consistency in both directions, and an inconsistent fixture would be rejected for THAT reason first, leaving the key-type divergence unmeasured while the case still appeared to cover it.
cases.yaml:
pins:
  did:key:zA:
    address: "777"
    first_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    last_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
addresses:
  777: did:key:zA

error_substrings: has a key that is not a plain string

cases.name: same-identity-pinned-at-two-addresses
cases.note: The state an upgrade-on-first-sight migration leaves behind when it declines: one agent reachable at two addresses, pinned under its stable id at one and its did:key at the other. A stable id is one key and a pin carries one address, so these cannot be merged; migrating anyway overwrote the pin holding the other address and produced a store both loaders refuse (default-aanw). Both runtimes must accept this document and agree on it, which is what makes declining safe.
cases.yaml:
pins:
  did:aw:S:
    address: acme.com/bob
    stable_id: did:aw:S
    did_key: did:key:zD
    first_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    last_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  did:key:zD:
    address: acme.com/alice
    first_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    last_seen: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
addresses:
  acme.com/alice: did:key:zD
  acme.com/bob: did:aw:S
